text:
IncidentBot: Pager: High 5xx rate for customer Vespera (private VPC) in us-west-2 — ingress/egress errors, NLB target health flapping, potential SG change detected. Paging on-call: @Alice Oncall.
Maya Ops: @Alice can you take this? Vespera is in dedicated Private deployment (tenant-id vsp-23) — they report production impact.
Alice Oncall: ACKed. I’m looking at console metrics now. 5xx from their public-facing endpoint spiked ~09:12 UTC. NLB health checks show ~40% targets unhealthy across two AZs. Connection timeouts and TLS errors in logs.
Alice Oncall: Quick check - Route53 traffic policy shows primary weighted to nlb-vsp-primary (weight 100). No obvious TTL changes.
Vespera_SRE: We pushed a security group rule change at ~09:05 to lock down an internal range, didn’t touch route tables or NLB. We’re seeing failed deploys too.
Brandon SRE: Observed conntrack table growth on NAT instances for vsp-23 tenant during the spike. Could be connection floods from a downstream service.
Carla NetOps: Confirming NLB health: target-group arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:tg/vsp-primary shows UnhealthyCount 68/160. Failed checks show TLS handshake errors from 10.x.x.x subnets.
Dinesh Eng: Any recent model/serving rollout for this tenant? Canary today?
Vespera_SRE: Yes, a canary for a model-change was rolled at 08:58 but only to 10% of instances. We saw increased latency but not errors pre-09:10.
Alice Oncall: Hypothesis: canary caused backend process to open many ephemeral connections -> NAT exhaustion -> NLB health checks failing -> DNS timed failovers. We'll triage in parallel: (1) contain traffic, (2) restore healthy targets, (3) confirm customer-facing recovery.
Maya Ops: Priority actions: get a mitigation path that avoids full rollback first. @Carla can you prepare a DNS weight shift to backup NLB and standby a conntrack purge plan? @Brandon run a quick conntrack snapshot. @Vespera_SRE hold any further deploys.
Carla NetOps: Ready to shift weights. Proposed immediate mitigation: Route53 weighted failover: primary->nlb-vsp-primary weight 0, backup->nlb-vsp-backup weight 100. TTL 30s. Will apply in 2 mins if approved.
Emma Support: Notifying Vespera PM & customer-facing channel that we’re executing failover with minimal downtime window.
Brandon SRE: Conntrack dump shows 95% table full on nat-1 and nat-2 for tenant vsp-23 (flow entries spike from one source subnet: 10.42.77.0/24). Likely a misbehaving canary instance.
Alice Oncall: Approve DNS weight shift. Execute now please and keep TTL low. Also add temporary iptables rule on NATs to drop established flows from 10.42.77.0/24 for this tenant while we identify the offending host (short-lived block, documented).
Carla NetOps: Applying Route53 change now:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1234 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.vespera.corp","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"vsp-backup","Weight":100,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZNLBFORBACKUP","DNSName":"nlb-vsp-backup-xxxx.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":false}}]}}'
```
Carla NetOps: Change submitted — propagating. TTL 30s.
Dinesh Eng: While DNS shifts, we should take the canary hosts out of the target group. @Vespera_SRE can you give instance IDs or node IDs for the canary?
Vespera_SRE: Canary nodes: node-vsp-canary-03, node-vsp-canary-04. Rolling back canary now.
Brandon SRE: Pushing conntrack policy:
```
# on nat instances
sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.42.77. | wc -l
sudo conntrack -D -s 10.42.77.0/24
```
Brandon SRE: Cleared conntrack entries for that subnet and added temporary iptables reject for 60s to throttle reconnection storm.
Alice Oncall: NLB target healthy count recovering on us-west-2a/2b. Health checks back to normal within 90s after conntrack purge. Metrics show 5xx count dropping.
Carla NetOps: Route53 shows traffic now resolving to nlb-vsp-backup as expected. Early telemetry: latency improved and 5xx rate down 85%.
Emma Support: Customer-facing update sent: "We detected an elevated error rate and executed a temporary failover to backup gateway while we isolate the root cause. Service is restored for most users. Engineers are investigating remaining edge cases."
Vespera_SRE: Canary rollback complete. The bad process was a new client connection loop in the model server. We’re shipping a fix to the canary code; full redeploy paused until postmortem.
Maya Ops: Good containment. Next steps: (1) keep backup NLB as primary for 30 minutes to validate, (2) rotate NAT instances if conntrack anomalies reoccur, (3) plan for controlled redeploy with rate-limits.
Dinesh Eng: We'll instrument extra connection caps and add graceful connection backoff in the model service. Dinesh will own follow-up fix and canary gating.
Brandon SRE: Removing temporary iptables block now. Conntrack levels stable.
Alice Oncall: Final check: affected user sessions ~6% at peak; initial estimate of customer impact: partial degradation for ~12 minutes. Full restore at ~09:28 UTC.
Emma Support: Logged a support incident & notified account team. Customer requested postmortem and timeline.
Maya Ops: Assigning follow-ups:
- Dinesh Eng: Root cause fix and hardened canary gating (ticket INF-4823)
- Brandon SRE: NAT conntrack monitoring + auto-throttle playbook (INF-4824)
- Carla NetOps: DNS playbook refinement + pre-warming backup NLB (INF-4825)
- Emma Support: Customer comms & postmortem draft (INF-4826)
Vespera_SRE: Thanks team. Appreciate the quick failover. We'll coordinate on the fix and tests.
Maya Ops: Incident declared resolved. Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Please add logs/commands used to the ticket.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved — closing runbook. Severity: Sev2. Duration: 00:16:18.
Alice Oncall: Adding quick notes: avoid immediate full conntrack purge unless scoped to tenant-subnet; prefer targeted conntrack deletes + short DNS failover.
Dinesh Eng: Adding fix PR link in INF-4823 and test plan.
Emma Support: Postmortem email drafted, will send once we have the timeline and attachments.
Carla NetOps: Saving Route53 change ID and NLB target-group diffs to incident artifacts.
Maya Ops: Thanks all — good coordination.
